_comment: Normal mode's setup-screen vocabulary: what a model may use when it writes a new employee's setup screen. The prompt's catalogue rules are written from this file into genui_prompt.txt (`bun run genui:prompts`; a client test fails while that file is stale), and the client's renderer imports its lists (client/src/features/home/genui/catalog.ts, hirePayload.ts); a client test holds the renderer's prop schemas to these components and props. A component marked `inserted` is added by the client's normalizer, never by the model, so the prompt leaves it out. `trigger.times` are the times a schedule can run at and `trigger.days` the days, in week order (services/employees/builder.py SCHEDULE_TIMES and WEEKDAYS, checked by tests/test_genui_catalog_sync.py). spec_version 2 is json-render's shape: a Toggle binds `checked`, and a Button's action is the element's `on.press` ({action, params}); the client still reads the older `value` and `action`/`actionParams` a model may write.

Card.description: Surface grouping related content. Has children.

Metric.description: A single number or fact to highlight.

Plan.description: An automation shown as a chain of steps: trigger first ("When…"), then agent/tool steps. A step that uses an app names it in "app".

Schedule.description: When they work, as a sentence the owner can change: what starts the work, and for a schedule how often and when. Seeded from the hire button's trigger.

AgentCard.description: An AI employee and what it does.

List.description: A list of emails, events, tasks or results.

Draft.description: A message ready for the user to approve.

Toggle.description: On/off ground rule, bound to state under /rules.

Choice.description: Pick one of 2-4 options, bound to state under /choices.

Input.description: Short text field, bound to state under /inputs.

Button.description: Runs an action, named beside its props: "on":{"press":{"action", "params"?}}.

actions.hire_employee: {name, role, apps:[string], trigger, sendsVia} — add this employee to the team and start them working
actions.refine: {} — let the owner describe a change to this setup
